kurz: Above a certain temperature, fat starts to smoke and break down. It then tastes bitter and irritates the eyes and throat.
bild_im_kopf: Like an engine revving into the red: it still runs, but it is taking damage.
was_passiert: Every fat can only take a certain heat. Above it, its components break down, visible smoke appears and it tastes bitter. Refined oils can take more than cold-pressed ones because suspended particles have been removed. Butter burns early because its milk proteins turn black even at medium heat.
warum_wichtig: For hard searing and deep-frying you need a fat that can take the heat. For flavour, butter goes in at the end.
faustregeln: For deep-frying, use refined oil, such as frying oil or high-oleic rapeseed oil.
Add butter only at the end for [[arosieren|basting]], or use clarified butter.
If it smokes, it is too hot: turn the heat down, and replace the oil if it has smoked a lot.

praxis.text: Deep-frying at 160–190 °C calls for an oil that can take a lot more.
Sear hard in oil, then add butter and herbs at the end.
